title: Introduce hyperseed defaults orchestrator and quant-anchor
author: Leah Park
description: Context & motivation: We've seen recurring customer asks and internal playbook churn around tenant warmup, sensible batch/cache defaults, and consistent quantization profiles during rollouts. Ad-hoc scripts and manual onboarding have produced subtle unit-econ regressions (ENG-2145). This PR introduces a small, composable orchestrator (hyperseed) and a companion CLI (hyperseedctl) that: (1) seeds tenant-level default batch/cache parameters based on sample traffic shapes, (2) applies an immutable 'quant-anchor' profile to model deployment metadata to ensure predictable inference cost paths during canary rollouts, and (3) emits unit-econ telemetry events so downstream billing/forecasting can attribute warmup costs. High-level changes: - New service: src/orchestrator/hyperseed.go implements an idempotent seed flow with safe-readback and tenant-scoped locks. - CLI: cmd/hyperseedctl with 'plan/apply/dry-run' subcommands and JSON/YAML profile import. - Quant-anchor: controlled metadata blob attached to model manifests; runtime checks enforce fallback when an incompatible quant profile would be selected. - Defaults catalog: data/defaults/catalog.json (compact, balanced, latency-first presets) plus a small selector that maps traffic percentiles -> batch/cache suggestion. - Telemetry: emit econ.seed.* events and tag traces with tenant.seed.variant. - Safety & rollbacks: seed is opt-in; a 'revert' command and automatic rollback if the runtime surface error rate increases beyond threshold. What this is not: hyperseed is not an autoscaler replacement or a global policy engine — it's focused on seeding safe defaults and attaching quant-anchor metadata for predictable cost behavior. Implementation notes & design tradeoffs: - The orchestrator collects a short 5-minute sample of request size/seq distribution from the tenant's recent traces (or accepts a supplied sample file) and runs a lightweight heuristic to choose batch_size, prefill_window, kv_cache_retention. - Quant-anchor supports three tiers: preserved-fp16, safe-int8, compact-quant (post-training calibration suggested). Anchors are intentionally conservative to avoid quality regressions during canaries. - We added an opt-in 'economics' mode which annotates profiles with estimated tokens-per-dollar using last-7-day price curves; this is only advisory in the first rollout. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-2145 - [x] CLI with plan/apply/dry-run/revert - [x] Runtime guard to refuse incompatible quant anchors - [x] Telemetry + basic dashboards (prefill heatmap, econ.seed trends) - [x] Unit + integration tests for idempotency + rollback plan - [x] Load tests demonstrating <2% p99 latency regression on moderate traffic Summary of test results: - Unit tests: 98% coverage on new packages. - Integration: staged on dedicated dev cluster for 48h with a synthetic mixed-load profile; CPU/GPU utilization unchanged within noise, observed warmup token cost increase of ~6% on first 10 minutes but steady-state improvement of ~3% token cost per request for low-compute tenants. - Canary: 5 tenants ran hyperseed in canary mode for 72h; no quality regressions; two tenants with heavy long-context traffic were suggested 'balanced' instead of 'compact' by the selector. How to use: - Plan: hyperseedctl plan --tenant <id> --sample sample.json - Apply (dry-run): hyperseedctl apply --tenant <id> --profile compact-warmup --dry-run - Apply: hyperseedctl apply --tenant <id> --profile compact-warmup - Revert: hyperseedctl revert --tenant <id> --since 2026-02-20 Rollback plan: - If post-seed error-rate increases >1% absolute or p99 latency degrades >10% relative for 30m, the operator-run hook will auto-trigger a revert and flag the tenant for manual inspection. Observability: - econ.seed.* metrics, new dashboard panels under Console -> Prefill -> Hyperseed. - New tags: tenant.seed.variant, tenant.seed.profile, quant.anchor.id Related work & references: - ENG-2145 (seed defaults playbook), ENG-2190 (quant anchor RFC). - Smaller companion PRs will follow to add tenant onboarding templates to the quickstarts repo. Security & compliance: - No secrets added. CLI requires operator role; RBAC checks in orchestrator code. Performance considerations: - Orchestrator runs as a low-priority job in the control plane; sampling window is configurable. - We intentionally limit per-tenant parallelism to 2 concurrent seed runs to avoid thundering. Migration notes: - Existing tenants who want to opt-in can run hyperseedctl. Nothing changes by default. - Operators can run a tenant-batch to seed on a schedule for low-touch onboarding. Open questions & next steps: - Expand quant-anchor tiers after collecting more evals. - Consider a 'shadow-apply' mode that applies defaults in the control plane but doesn't modify the runtime until confirmed.

release_notes: Adds hyperseed orchestrator and hyperseedctl CLI to seed tenant defaults and attach conservative quant-anchor profiles. Opt-in; adds telemetry for unit-econ attribution and a small dashboard. No default behavior changes. CLI and control-plane safeguards included.
files_preview: src/orchestrator/hyperseed.go: seedTenant(tenantID string) -> collects sample, chooses profile, writes metadata. cmd/hyperseedctl/main.go: subcommands plan|apply|dry-run|revert. internal/quant/anchor.go: ValidateAnchorCompatibility(manifest, anchor) with safe fallback path. data/defaults/catalog.json: three presets with suggested batch/cache/kv retention values.
